question: Will Argentina's Senate pass the 'Super RIGI' bill before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Deputies passed the Super RIGI on June 24, 2026 (130-106). The Senate referred it to three committees, and they have been stuck since Sept 2 with no dictamen. Allies Abad, Espínola, Goerling and Huala demand a 15% price preference for local suppliers, and per Infobae on Oct 12 the Economy Ministry has not accepted it. Bullrich has floated keeping the original RIGI instead. About 9 weeks remain; ordinary sessions end in late November, and December extraordinary sessions look likely but center on the 2027 Budget and political reform. The bill passes if the government concedes the local-content clause and puts it on the Dec agenda. That concession is fairly small and the government has used extraordinaries before, so Yes is plausible but not the base case. No prediction market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi searched; Polymarket is blocked in Argentina).
calls.dossier:
- Senate file 6-CD-26 (senado.gob.ar): Deputies passed it June 24, 2026; the Senate received it July 16; referred to Budget & Treasury, National Economy & Investment, and General Legislation committees. No dictamen listed.
- Deputies vote, June 2026 (hcdn.gob.ar via search): 130 for, 106 against, 7 abstentions.
- Aug 27, 2026 (lu24): government called the Super RIGI its immediate Senate priority for September; the Senate is described as the agenda's main bottleneck.
- Sept 1-2, 2026 (tiempoar, shale24, parlamentario, iprofesional): the joint committee session added changes (energy-supply requirement for electricity-heavy projects; 20% floor for national suppliers) and opened the text for signatures, but the session ended with no report. Allies Abad (UCR), Espínola (dissident Peronist), Goerling (PRO), later Huala (PRO), asked for a 15% price margin for local suppliers; 7 allied senators were absent. A Sept 17 floor date was floated, then lapsed.
- Bullrich, Sept 2026: 'if the Super RIGI has so many problems, we stay with the RIGI.'
- Oct 12, 2026 (Infobae): still paralyzed; the Casa Rosada and Economy Ministry have not accepted the allies' demands; no deal without them. A similar dispute is holding up the RIIR regime.
- Oct 19, 2026 (Ámbito): still stalled. Ordinary deliberation runs to about Nov 20; after that, only extraordinary sessions called by the president, or nothing until March 1, 2027. Extraordinary sessions are expected mainly for the 2027 Budget (Deputies vote set for Nov 18) and political reform; the papal visit and officials' travel squeeze the calendar.
- Oct 26, 2026 (mdzol headline): friction between Bullrich and Milei; government cancelled its political-strategy meeting.
- Rule: 7 days must pass between dictamen and floor vote unless two-thirds waive it. Senate amendments send the bill back to Deputies, which still counts as YES under the fine print.
- Precedent: Milei's government has used December/February extraordinary sessions for priority bills (labor reform got its Senate dictamen in Dec 2025 but reached the floor only in February).
- Status-quo outcome: no Senate floor vote before Jan 1, 2027.
- Resolution instrument: resolves on the Senate floor approving the bill in general AND in particular, not on a committee report or presidential signature.
- Event window: the question was created (date unknown) -> before Jan 1, 2027. As of Oct 27, 2026, about 9.5 weeks remain.
- Searched but not found: any news from Oct 20-27 on a deal, a new dictamen date, or the Super RIGI being listed in an extraordinary-sessions decree; no prediction market (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi).

calls.dossier:
- Deputies approved the Super RIGI (incentives for investments of at least USD 1bn in 'new industries': AI/data centers, semiconductors, green hydrogen, lithium batteries, etc.). It is now under review in the Senate (expediente 6.26/CD/PL). Sources: search summaries, Grant Thornton background, iProfesional, Aug-Sep 2026.
- Aug 2026: the Senate began debate in a joint session of three committees (Budget & Finance, National Economy & Investment, General Legislation). LLA originally aimed for a floor vote around Sept 9-10. Sources: Parlamentario 2026-08-03, ADNSUR.
- Sept 2, 2026: the committee report failed to get signatures in all three committees. Abad (UCR-BA), Espínola (dissident PJ-Corrientes), Goerling (PRO-Misiones) and Huala (PRO-La Pampa) refused to sign. They demanded a preference of up to 15% for national suppliers, raising the 'compre nacional' share from 20% to 40%, price comparison on a delivered-to-destination basis, and consulting local companies before declaring insufficient domestic supply. Sources: MDZ, iProfesional, El Cronista, 2026-09-02.
- Sept 2026: LLA then targeted a floor vote on Sept 17. That did not happen. Bullrich called the 15% demand 'at the margin of libertarian philosophy'. Caputo's ministry did not send officials. Sources: iProfesional 09-02, Letra P, El Destape.
- Oct 4, 2026 (Infobae): stalled since early September. An unnamed senator said there is currently no clear path to the floor. The government might settle for keeping only the existing RIGI.
- Oct 12, 2026 (Infobae headline): no deal unless the Casa Rosada accepts the allies' demands.
- Oct 18, 2026 (Infobae): the Economy Ministry sent the allies a counterproposal (price comparison at equivalent delivered prices; consult business before declaring insufficient domestic supply). Unclear whether it meets all demands. Infobae said the government has less than 1.5 months of ordinary sessions left and would need 'magic' to finish its agenda.
- Oct 26, 2026 (El Destape): LLA focus this week is the 2027 Budget committee report in Deputies (floor vote targeted Nov 4) and a Senate session on Oct 29 (Mental Health law, patents treaty, carbon market, judicial nominations). The Super RIGI is not mentioned. The Senate would then have a few weeks in November for the Budget, political reform and the Super RIGI.
- Procedure: needs a signed committee report (or 2/3 to bring it to the floor without one), then approval in general and in particular. Any Senate amendments send it back to Deputies, which still counts as YES under the fine print.
- Calendar: ordinary sessions end Nov 30. Extraordinary sessions (precedent: Dec 10-30, 2025 by presidential decree) need the bill on the executive's agenda.
- Status quo: not passed (stalled at committee).
- Resolves on an Argentine Senate floor vote approving in general and in particular (senado.gob.ar record), not on the committee report or on Deputies.
- Event window: now -> 2027-01-01 per the criteria. The window effectively runs from Deputies approval, so most of the period has elapsed; about 9 weeks remain as of 2026-10-27.
- Searched but not found: the allies' response to the Oct 18 counterproposal; any signed committee report after Sept 2; a scheduled Super RIGI floor date; the December extraordinary-session agenda for 2026; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).
- Base-rate note: no published rate. Roughly, Milei-era priority bills stalled in Senate committee over allied demands have sometimes been unblocked in end-of-year extraordinary sessions after concessions, and other times left pending or dropped. No counted dataset was found.

calls.reasoning: Deputies passed the Super RIGI in June 2026. Senate committees have been stuck since Sept 2 at 20 of 26 signatures because allies Abad, Espínola, Goerling and Huala demanded a 15% preference for national suppliers. The Oct 18 Economy Ministry counterproposal largely concedes that 15% margin, so the substantive gap has narrowed. Still, by Oct 25 nothing had been signed, tensions over broken promises were rising, and senators called even December passage a 'miracle'. Ordinary sessions end late November; December extraordinary sessions would need the executive to include the bill, with the 2027 Budget taking priority. The status quo of no vote by Jan 1 remains more likely, but a deal followed by a quick report and floor vote is a real path.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) whether the Oct 18 counterproposal met the allies' 15% demand. Runs 1 and 2 thought it unaccepted or unclear; Run 3 said it largely met it. My search of the Infobae Oct 18 article shows its text includes the 15% price margin, so the substantive gap has largely closed, which favors Run 3. (2) Whether the allies accepted or a committee report was signed after Oct 18. Searches for October signatures and the counterproposal turned up nothing after Sept 2, and Infobae Oct 25 still called it a mystery, with tension and senators calling December passage a 'miracle'. So this is not settled, and the status quo holds. (3) Calendar and extraordinary sessions: Ámbito says extraordinary sessions are increasingly likely, but nothing has been decreed. Judgment: the narrowed gap raises the odds above Runs 1 and 2, while the lack of progress and the time squeeze keep it below Run 3's 0.38. Market check: none found.
